what_this_is: Six slambench.run shards produced on the space-container A100 pod against ego-synth 5B, at #020's own split digest 61195914f090. They add two things #020 does not have: a cross-box control on 84 of #020's own cells, and 48 new cells -- the multi-frame context arms at STRIDE 1, which #020 never ran. This is NOT the FOV/eccentricity work ticket 022 asks for; that is slambench.run_fov and is a separate run.
why_it_is_published_late: The runs finished 2026-08-20 with rc=0 on every shard and were left in the pod's eval_out. autoresearch/findings.md already cites their stride-10 conclusion (commit 60790fa, H11 temporal re-scope), so the numbers were read and acted on while the artefacts were on no branch -- which the tickets README explicitly forbids ('Status is derived from what is on the results branch, not from memory'). Publishing them closes that gap rather than adding a new claim.
hardware: space-container pod run1156075-vggt-omega-360, 2x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB, one lane per card

env.note: cu128 deliberately, matching lambda_63. The site pip mirror serves a +cu130 wheel that runs fine and is a different numerical stack; SPACE_CONTAINER.md section 2 covers why that must be asserted rather than assumed.

split.oxford: absent, as in #020 -- its sensor-to-upright rotation has never been measured
split.egoexo4d: absent, as in #020 -- paused by owner decision

sharded.by: model, across the two A100s; shards/ holds the six raw results.json
sharded.why_this_is_exact: slambench.run computes the support intersection INSIDE its per-model loop, over that model's own arms and contexts, so two processes with disjoint model lists produce the numbers one process would. This is #020's own argument and it is unchanged here.
sharded.step2.g1_was_backfilled: step2.g1's first attempt produced no results.json; it was re-run to completion as step2.g1.backfill (rc=0). Both logs are kept in logs/.

step3-s1.what: the context sweep at STRIDE 1 -- new, #020 has no such arms

step3-s10.what: the context sweep at STRIDE 10 -- overlaps #020, and is the cross-box control

cross_box_control.what_was_compared: every cell of this run that is also a cell of results/slambench-020-143686a -- 84 of them -- matched on (model, dataset, baseline, context, context_stride)
cross_box_control.reading: Not bit-identical and never could be -- a different GPU architecture reorders floating-point reductions. Mean 0.15% and worst 1.28% on AbsRel is an order below the 3-40% context effects this harness measures, so a pod number may be tabulated beside a lambda one. It is not zero, so the two boxes must not be mixed inside a single curve.

headline.claim: multi-frame context pays only with temporal distance, on real MPS SLAM points
headline.stride_1: 24 arms, AbsRel ratio against their own N=1 spans 0.957-1.157, mean 1.017 -- adjacent frames cost slightly more than they pay, and 10 frames is usually the worst of the three
headline.stride_10: 24 arms, ratio spans 0.867-1.086, mean 0.981 -- the same frame counts now help; best cell da3_large / nymeria / rect_derect / 10 frames at 0.867
headline.mechanism_consistent_with: baseline, not frame count. Consecutive frames of a head-mounted camera are ~1 cm apart against several metres of scene -- no parallax, so the extra views add compute and no geometry. Stride 10 buys ~9 cm.
headline.independent_of: the same conclusion #001 recorded for ScanNet++ evaluation stride, reached here on different data with a different ground truth

not_claimed: This does not replace #020. #020 remains the published SLAM baseline table; this is a control beside it plus the stride-1 arms it lacks.
No eccentricity axis anywhere in this run -- these are whole-image averages. The FOV question on these same points is ticket 022's slambench.run_fov work and is a separate artefact.
The 84-cell agreement is a control on this harness at this split; it does not license mixing boxes inside one curve.
Why da3_small / nymeria / rect_derect is the worst-agreeing cell is not established.
